title: Fitness cost, compensation, and why RR-TB still spreads
dek: A resistance mutation can slow growth in broth and still succeed in a cavity and a city if compensation, bottleneck, and transmission repair the cost. Competitive index ≠ a DST column.
story: Many resistance mutations have a fitness cost in vitro: slower doubling, a smaller competitive index against wild type in mixed culture, fewer insertions in a TnSeq pool. rpoB S450L is costly for RNAP until rpoC/rpoA compensation retunes the enzyme. Some pncA LOF alleles look cheap; some gyrA alleles look expensive. Cost is allele-specific, not a property of the word “resistant.”

Cost in 7H9 is not cost in a cavity. Mutation supply scales with burden; a small defect can be paid for by a huge population. Once a compensated clone is airborne, epidemiology can dominate broth rankings. That is why S450L lineages are global and why “resistant strains cannot transmit” is a 1990s sentence.

Computational genomics: fitness is a covariate for which alleles you expect to see, and a reason compensatory RNAP sites belong in outbreak masks or not depending on the question. It is not a reason to down-grade a high-confidence rpoB hit because the strain “looks fit.”
deepTitle: How cost is measured, and how it is misused
deep: Competitive index: mix WT and mutant, compare ratios before and after outgrowth. A CI of 0.5 is a cost; it is not 50% lower MIC.
TnSeq fitness (resampling between conditions) is a pool-relative number, not a clinical prognosis.
Compensation can be epistatic and lineage-dependent. Importing an L4 rpoC story into L2 without looking is a prior, not a result.
Within-host: a costly allele can still rise under drug pressure. After treatment stops, a fitter revertant or a compensated sister can take over. Serial isolates are the movie; one genome is a still.

visual.caption: Schematic growth-rate distributions: wild-type broth, uncompensated S450L shifted left (cost), compensated RR restored toward WT. Transmission success can still follow the compensated mound even if a lab CI looked grim last decade.

example.title: CI 0.4 and a city outbreak
example.setup: A lab measures competitive index 0.4 for a new rpoB allele versus H37Rv in 7H9. A programme officer concludes the allele cannot cause an outbreak. City WGS already shows a 40-isolate cluster with that allele plus rpoC compensation.

steps.title: Broth ≠ city
steps.body: CI 0.4 is a real cost in that assay. Compensation and airborne transmission are extra parameters. The cluster is the epidemiologic likelihood.

steps.title: Do not un-call DST
steps.body: The rpoB allele still grades R. Fitness is not a susceptibility column.

steps.title: Use cost as a prior for which alleles spread
steps.body: Cheap, compensated alleles are the ones you expect to see globally. Expensive, uncompensated alleles may stay in one patient. That is a prior for genomic epi, not a reason to skip contact investigation.

example.takeaway: Fitness cost is real, allele-specific, and not a transmission off-switch.

check.prompt: A competitive index of 0.5 for a resistant mutant versus wild type in broth means:
choices: The mutant was at a growth disadvantage in that assay, not that it cannot transmit in a city
check.answer: The mutant was at a growth disadvantage in that assay, not that it cannot transmit in a city
check.why: CI is an in-vitro ratio. Compensated RR-TB outbreaks exist.

check.prompt: rpoB S450L is common worldwide partly because:
choices: It is silent and therefore cost-free always
It is tolerated relative to some other RRDR alleles and is often paired with compensatory RNAP mutations that restore fitness
Xpert cannot see it, so it spreads undetected only
check.answer: It is tolerated relative to some other RRDR alleles and is often paired with compensatory RNAP mutations that restore fitness
check.why: The rpoC plate is this sentence. Cost is not infinite.

whyWrong.It is silent and therefore cost-free alw: S450L is missense and can be costly until compensated.
whyWrong.Xpert cannot see it, so it spreads undet: Xpert is built around RRDR; S450L is the celebrity hit.

check.prompt: On the density plate, the compensated-RR curve sits near wild-type to show:
choices: Compensation can restore growth toward WT without undoing the rpoB resistance mechanism
Compensation erases rpoB from the genome
check.answer: Compensation can restore growth toward WT without undoing the rpoB resistance mechanism
check.why: Secondary RNAP alleles retune the enzyme. They are not a second RRDR for Xpert.

whyWrong.WT cannot grow: WT is the rightmost/fast mound here.
